extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers (and applicants) for Research Project Grant mechanisms (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and explanatory guidance for peer review of NIH Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), describing the criteria reviewers should use to score and critique applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overall impact score synthesizes judgment across the criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) and any additional review criteria. It reflects the likelihood the project will have a sustained, powerful influence on the field(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact/Priority (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution to the research field(s) involved, to provide research opportunities to students, and to strengthen the research environment of the institution, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 (AREA) applications the overall impact/prioritization explicitly includes the potential effect on the school/institution (strengthening research environment, exposing students to research) in addition to scientific contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Research Grant (R03) evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding. Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach to the problem. Appropriate justification can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Research Enhancement Award (R15) evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of the R15 program: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students to meritorious research. Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider both scientific merit and the programmatic goals of strengthening research environment and student exposure; preliminary data optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant (R21) evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact. An R21 need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge. Appropriate justification can be provided via literature, other-source data, or investigator data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant (R34) evaluation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials (establishment of team, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, finalization of protocol, operations manual). The R34 is not designed for collection of preliminary data or conduct of pilot studies to support rationale for a trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 also consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will have a substantial effect on the school/academic component in terms of strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or those in early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, consider whether investigators have complementary and integrated expertise and whether leadership approach, governance and organizational structure are appropriate. For R15, also consider whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and will risky aspects be managed? If human subjects/clinical research are involved, evaluate plans for protection of human subjects and inclusion/exclusion of individuals by sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children, justified in terms of scientific goals and strategy. For R15 clinical research wording parallels R01 guidance. For R15 also consider whether the application provides sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available adequate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the project will benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements. For R15, consider availability of well-qualified students and evidence that students have in the past or are likely to pursue careers in the biomedical or behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that meets criteria for one or more of the six exempt categories under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate: 1) justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as the inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if it is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: 1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; 2) justifications for the use of animals and for appropriateness of species and numbers proposed; 3) adequacy of veterinary care; 4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable including use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, determine whether adequate protection is proposed (biosafety, containment, training, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should weigh how well prior criticisms were addressed and whether revisions adequately respond to previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accomplishments to date, productivity, and whether the renewal's aims are justified by prior progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision application relates to a specific line of investigation from the original application that was not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to previous comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether foreign-based resources or conditions materially enhance the project's scientific merit or opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application, including: 1) the Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research, 2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, 3) the procedures that will be used to monitor possession use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and 4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness and adequacy of institutional registration, monitoring and biosafety/biocontainment/security plans for working with select agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing the following types of resources, are reasonable: 1) Data Sharing Plan; 2) Sharing Model Organisms; and 3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on reasonableness of plans or the justification for not sharing; these comments inform program staff and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether requested resources are appropriate to accomplish the aims and whether the duration requested is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional narrative feedback to help applicants improve; may include suggestions, concerns, or recommendation not to resubmit in current form.
